set.st: "Old Whit" Knaggs, one of the county's first settlers, kept a trading post and was said to have gathered gold from land speculators; he buried it along the Shiawassee River just south of Knaggs' Bridge. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. Knaggs' hill is on the E (right) bank; Gaylord Cemetery adjoins it: look-only near the cemetery. 1873 atlas places the crossing beside the Shiawassee treaty reserve. 1936: Knaggs gully near the bridge, dug over many times. The earliest telling found (Michigan Pioneer and Historical Collections, 1902) says Whitmore Knaggs buried speculators' money around Knaggs Bridge on the Shiawassee. A man named Hadd dug for it about twenty years later, and before the Civil War parties dug at night by a map that marked 'the rock, the tree, and the spring' (E. O. Byam showed them the spring). It names storekeeper Thomas B. Allen, and says the post site then belonged to Hon. N. G. Phillips. The 1906 county history ('Shiawassee's Captain Kidd') adds that the searchers asked after 'a rock in the river known as Indian Rock'; no Indian Rock is named in GNIS, and the rock is not yet located.
